LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_FOUR.learnerPromise: Offer a possible solution or ask whether an action is permitted.
LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_FOUR.explanation: 可以 can suggest a possible solution or give permission. Ask with 可以…嗎 or 可不可以; answer permission questions with 可以 or 不可以.

teachingGlossary.meaning: may or may not; can or cannot
go watch it at the movie theater
use or play on a phone
shows belonging or links a describing word

LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_FOUR.pattern: Person + 可以 + action / 可以…嗎？

discoveryLab.title: Read the green-light card
discoveryLab.description: The same 可以 either opens a possible path or checks permission.
discoveryLab.prompt: What job is 可以 doing?

choices.label: Suggestion
choices.note: A problem comes first; 可以 offers one useful option.

choices.label: Ask permission
choices.english: May I go to the restroom?
choices.note: The speaker asks whether the action has a green light.

choices.label: No permission
choices.traditional: 不可以在捷運上吃東西。
choices.simplified: 不可以在捷运上吃东西。
choices.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi.
choices.english: Eating on the metro is not allowed.

choices.label: Repair order
choices.traditional: 我去可以嗎 → 我可以去嗎
choices.simplified: 我去可以吗 → 我可以去吗
choices.pinyin: Wǒ qù kěyǐ ma → Wǒ kěyǐ qù ma
choices.note: Put 可以 before the action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Problem + 可以 = possible solution. 可以…嗎 = permission check.

contrast.title: Skill 會 vs. green-light 可以
contrast.description: Both can translate as “can,” but they answer different questions.

items.label: Permission
items.note: 可以 asks whether swimming is allowed.

patternRows.english: You could order a cup of hot tea.
We could go watch it together.
May I go to the restroom?

items.question: May I go to the restroom? Can I say 去洗手間可以嗎?
items.answer: No — 可以 goes before the action word: 我可以去洗手間嗎？

right.english: May I go to the restroom?

items.question: To ask Mom if I may have ice cream, can I say 我想吃冰淇淋嗎?
items.answer: No — 想 means want. To ask permission, use 可以: 我可以吃冰淇淋嗎？

items.question: Do I add 嗎 after 可不可以, like 可以不可以去嗎?
items.answer: No — 可不可以 is already a question. Adding 嗎 doubles the question ending.

right.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ qù kàn diànyǐng ma?
right.english: Can we go see a movie?

text.traditional: A：對不起，我不喝咖啡。 B：沒關係，你可以點一杯熱茶。
text.simplified: A：对不起，我不喝咖啡。 B：没关系，你可以点一杯热茶。
text.pinyin: A: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ bù hē kāfēi. B: Méiguānxi, nǐ kěyǐ diǎn yì bēi rè chá.
text.english: A: Sorry, I do not drink coffee. B: No problem. You could order hot tea.

text.traditional: A：媽媽，我可以吃冰淇淋嗎？ B：太冷了，不可以。
text.simplified: A：妈妈，我可以吃冰淇淋吗？ B：太冷了，不可以。
text.pinyin: A: Māma, wǒ kěyǐ chī bīngqílín ma? B: Tài lěng le, bù kěyǐ.
text.english: A: Mom, may I eat ice cream? B: It is too cold. No.

text.traditional: A：我們可不可以在捷運上吃東西？ B：不可以，也不可以喝飲料。
text.simplified: A：我们可不可以在捷运上吃东西？ B：不可以，也不可以喝饮料。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen kě bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi? B: Bù kěyǐ, yě bù kěyǐ hē yǐnliào.
text.english: A: May we eat on the metro? B: No. Drinking is not allowed either.

LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: Describe a small, often inconvenient degree: a little tired, cold, or small.
LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Put 有一點兒 or 有點兒 right before a describing word to mean “a little.” It often softens a problem or an unwanted feeling. Do not add 很 after it.

teachingGlossary.meaning: may or may not; can or cannot
go watch it at the movie theater
use or play on a phone
shows belonging or links a describing word

LESSON_SIX_GRAMMAR_THREE.pattern: Person or thing + 有（一）點（兒） + describing word

discoveryLab.title: Turn up only one notch
discoveryLab.description: The dial makes the describing word softer — often before you explain a problem or say no.
discoveryLab.prompt: What kind of small problem appears?

choices.label: Feeling
choices.note: A mild feeling explains why rest may help.

choices.label: Evaluation
choices.english: The coffee is a little expensive.
choices.note: It is a little expensive, so you may choose another place.

choices.label: Reservation
choices.english: The clothes are a little small.
choices.note: The clothes look nice, but they are a little small.

choices.label: Repair order
choices.traditional: 我累有點兒 → 我有點兒累
choices.simplified: 我累有点儿 → 我有点儿累
choices.pinyin: Wǒ lèi yǒudiǎnr → Wǒ yǒudiǎnr lèi
choices.note: Put 有點兒 before the describing word.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Say who or what first, then 有點兒, then the describing word. One small notch, often for a mild problem.

contrast.title: A little vs. a little amount
contrast.description: 有點兒 softens a describing word. 點兒 after an action or a thing means a small amount.

items.label: Small degree
items.note: 有點兒 comes right before the describing word 渴.

items.label: Small amount
items.english: I want to drink a little beverage.
items.note: 點兒 measures a small amount of 飲料.

patternRows.english: The weather is a little cold.
This room is a little small.

items.question: This room is a little small. Do I need 是?
items.answer: No — 是 introduces who or what something is, not how it feels. Use 有一點兒 + 小.

right.pinyin: Zhè jiān fángjiān yǒu yìdiǎnr xiǎo.
right.english: This room is a little small.

items.question: Can I say 我有一點兒很累 to mean “very tired”?
items.answer: No — 有點兒 already does the degree job. It means “a little”, not “very”, so do not add 很.

items.question: The weather is a little cold. Is it 天氣冷有點兒?
items.answer: No — 有點兒 goes right before the describing word: 有點兒冷。

right.english: The weather is a little cold.

text.traditional: A：我們在這家咖啡廳喝咖啡吧。 B：一杯咖啡一百八十塊錢，我覺得有點兒貴。我們去那家吧。
text.simplified: A：我们在这家咖啡厅喝咖啡吧。 B：一杯咖啡一百八十块钱，我觉得有点儿贵。我们去那家吧。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen zài zhè jiā kāfēitīng hē kāfēi ba. B: Yì bēi kāfēi yì bǎi bāshí kuài qián, wǒ juéde yǒudiǎnr guì. Wǒmen qù nà jiā ba.
text.english: A: Let’s drink coffee at this café. B: A coffee costs 180 dollars. I think that is a little expensive. Let’s go to that place.

text.traditional: A：我們今天晚上去看電影，好不好？ B：今天我有點兒忙，我不想去。
text.simplified: A：我们今天晚上去看电影，好不好？ B：今天我有点儿忙，我不想去。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒmen jīntiān wǎnshang qù kàn diànyǐng, hǎo bù hǎo? B: Jīntiān wǒ yǒudiǎnr máng, wǒ bù xiǎng qù.
text.english: A: How about we see a movie tonight? B: I am a little busy today. I do not want to go.

text.traditional: A：這件衣服很漂亮，也很便宜，你不買嗎？ B：我很喜歡這件衣服，可是我覺得有點兒小。
text.simplified: A：这件衣服很漂亮，也很便宜，你不买吗？ B：我很喜欢这件衣服，可是我觉得有点儿小。
text.pinyin: A: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piàoliàng, yě hěn piányi, nǐ bù mǎi ma? B: Wǒ hěn xǐhuān zhè jiàn yīfu, kěshì wǒ juéde yǒudiǎnr xiǎo.
text.english: A: These clothes are very pretty and cheap. Why don’t you buy them? B: I like them very much, but I think they are a little small.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 找一個適合的活動時間 · Finding a workable activity time

text.traditional: 聽說這部電影很有趣，我們晚上一起去看，好不好？
text.simplified: 听说这部电影很有趣，我们晚上一起去看，好不好？
text.pinyin: Tīngshuō zhè bù diànyǐng hěn yǒuqù. Wǒmen wǎnshang yìqǐ qù kàn, hǎo bù hǎo?
text.english: I heard that this movie is very interesting. How about we go to see it tonight?

text.traditional: 我覺得有一點兒累，我想回家休息。
text.simplified: 我觉得有一点儿累，我想回家休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde yǒu yìdiǎnr lèi, wǒ xiǎng huí jiā xiūxí.
text.english: I am feeling a bit tired, I want to go home for a rest.

text.traditional: 你不要常常在家上網、看電腦、玩手機，應該去運動。明天我有空，我們可以一起去騎腳踏車。
text.simplified: 你不要常常在家上网、看电脑、玩手机，应该去运动。明天我有空，我们可以一起去骑脚踏车。
text.pinyin: Nǐ búyào chángcháng zài jiā shàngwǎng, kàn diànnǎo, wán shǒujī, yīnggāi qù yùndòng. Míngtiān wǒ yǒukòng, wǒmen kěyǐ yìqǐ qù qí jiǎotàchē.
text.english: Don’t surf the internet, use the computer or play on the cell phone at home often. You should go exercise. I am available tomorrow. We can go ride bikes together.

words.meaning: use or play on a phone

text.traditional: 可是我只想聽音樂、睡覺。
text.simplified: 可是我只想听音乐、睡觉。
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ zhǐ xiǎng tīng yīnyuè, shuìjiào.
text.english: But I only want to listen to music and sleep.
How about the day after tomorrow then?

text.traditional: 這兩天天氣有點兒冷，我們週末去，好嗎？
text.simplified: 这两天天气有点儿冷，我们周末去，好吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè liǎng tiān tiānqì yǒudiǎnr lěng, wǒmen zhōumò qù, hǎo ma?
text.english: It is a bit cold those two days. How about we do it this weekend?
